Progress Log

Newest entries first. Every implementation slice adds an entry. Append-only: never delete, never reorder, never edit a previous entry.

Each slice is an <article data-slice="..." data-date="YYYY-MM-DD"> with the following <dl> entries: Branch, PR, Changed, Verification, Assumptions, GDD coverage, Followups.

How to add a slice entry

Copy this template, fill in the values, and insert it as the new top entry under <main id="entries">.

<article data-slice="short-title" data-date="YYYY-MM-DD">
  <h3>Short Title</h3>
  <dl>
    <dt>Branch</dt><dd><code>feature/short-name</code></dd>
    <dt>PR</dt><dd>#N (when known)</dd>
    <dt>Changed</dt><dd>one paragraph naming the user-facing change and the key files / helpers / defaults that landed.</dd>
    <dt>Verification</dt><dd>dash checks, type-check, relevant unit tests, build, smoke (where applicable). Note any known-tolerated lint warnings or skipped checks.</dd>
    <dt>Assumptions</dt><dd>assumptions made under a Recommended default. One sentence per assumption.</dd>
    <dt>GDD coverage</dt><dd>which rows in <code>docs/GDD_COVERAGE.json</code> flipped to <code>partial</code> or <code>done</code>, or which <code>docs/gdd/*.html</code> files gained a Build log entry.</dd>
    <dt>Followups</dt><dd>any new <code>F-NNN</code> entries created. Link to them.</dd>
  </dl>
</article>

feat/bunker-stair-climb

Changed
Built the staircase climb, the crux the plan flagged as highest-risk ("no precedent for a ramp in the discrete-cell mover"). The user chose the ramp model (walk smoothly up one layer) over an auto-jump step-up or a ladder climb. The grid (bunker-fp-grid.ts) gains four walkable stair values (FP_STAIR_PX/PZ/NX/NZ) that encode the ascent direction, and buildFpSolidGrid stamps a stair-panel to the value for its orientation (the first reader of the orientation field from the data-model slice). The mover (bunker-fp-movement.ts) gains a per-frame ramp pass after the Y resolution: it finds the highest stair-ramp surface within reach of the feet in the capsule's column and clamps the feet onto it, so crossing a stair in its facing direction slopes you up one full layer and walking the other way descends, while a jump off a stair stays intact. Tighten the Full E2E deadline floor, override, upload, and triage query

fix/scheduled-e2e-deadline-visibility (same PR; an appended correction article, not an in-place edit of the committed article above).
PR
No package bump: CI harness and triage-doc corrections only, no app or player-facing behavior. (Rule 13) mine tips reviewed, no change; (Rule 14) no stamp.
Changed
A review round pressed five holds on the deadline-visibility slice plus an evidence-scope calibration; all are addressed. (1) Reserve floor: the earlier "floored at 60s so a pathological pre-test phase still gives the tests a minimum window" framing was wrong about intent. The floor (now 30s) exists ONLY to keep globalTimeout above 0, because Playwright treats globalTimeout: 0 as unlimited, which would re-introduce the job-deadline cancel. It is NOT a promise of upload room in the case where checkout/install/build already consumed the budget; that case loses evidence unavoidably and fails red regardless. (2) Override validation and clamp: the full_e2e_global_timeout_ms dispatch override was passed through unvalidated and uncapped. It is now rejected unless it is a positive integer, and clamped DOWN to the safe computed budget so a too-large override cannot re-introduce a cancel; a low override (the proof case) still passes through. (3) Upload permissiveness: the artifact upload dropped if-no-files-found: ignore for warn. The reporter always writes playwright-report/ on a failure, so the no-files case now only occurs when the report is genuinely absent, and warn keeps that evidence-loss visible in the log instead of silently succeeding with an empty upload. (4) Scheduled-run triage query: AGENTS.md and docs/CI_WORKFLOW.html used a client-side select(.event == "schedule") over the default run page, which silently returns null once a day of push and PR runs pushes the rare schedule run off the page (an empty result reads as "no red"). The query now filters server-side with gh run list --workflow CI --event schedule --limit 1. (5) Supersession rule: the earlier "a superseded cancellation stays ignorable" was too loose for scheduled Full E2E. A push or PR run on a newer main SHA does NOT supersede a scheduled timeout, because push and PR gates never run the Full E2E matrix; only a later scheduled run or a full_e2e dispatch that actually exercised the matrix on an equal-or-newer SHA supersedes it. Both docs now say so.
Verification
dash clean; git diff --check clean. The forced-timeout dispatch proof (run 29531137295) concluded failure with all four Full E2E shards failure (not cancelled) and all four artifacts retained, confirming the failure-not-cancel plus upload-runs mechanism end to end. Evidence calibration recorded honestly: a 30-second forced budget expires during startup before any test runs, so that artifact holds playwright-report/ (HTML + results.json) and one error-context.md per shard, not per-test traces or screenshots; traces (on-first-retry) and screenshots (on failure) exist only when tests actually run and fail, which a real slow-shard timeout with the full computed deadline produces. The guarantee is "always fails red, never cancels, always uploads whatever the reporter wrote, up to and including traces when the timeout lands mid-run."
Assumptions
The 30s floor never binds in normal operation (setup + build leave roughly 12 to 15 minutes, well above the floor); it binds only if the pre-test phase is broken, where evidence loss is already unavoidable and the run is red. Clamping the override down cannot break the proof case, which uses a value below the safe budget. Record every elevator rail buy in a durable, deduplicated outbox

Branch
fix/elevator-outbox-idempotency.
PR
No package bump: server and telemetry infrastructure plus a client idempotency key. Buys behave identically for the player (same charge, same response), so no release note and (Rule 13) the mine tips were reviewed with nothing to change; (Rule 14) no stamp (durable observability, not a player milestone).
Changed
Closes the second F-121 "Monitoring update": make the structured mutation outcome durable and deduplicated by tying a request id to the placement/extension transaction through a transactional outbox, so lost responses, duplicate delivery, request replay, and post-commit crash recovery still produce exactly one outcome per request without ever rolling back committed gameplay. New table elevator_upgrade_outcomes (src/server/db.ts): one row per request_id (unique), with operation, result, reason, and a nullable delivered_at, plus a partial index over undelivered rows for the drain. The client (buyRemoteElevator) now sends a fresh UUID requestId per buy (a param defaulting to a generated id, so a future lost-success retry can reuse it); a malformed or absent id is tolerated (the server mints one), so a legacy client still buys safely under the expectedDepth guard. The route (src/app/api/elevator/upgrade/route.ts) inserts the outcome row INSIDE each guarded-write CTE, gated on EXISTS (outcome_insert) with ON CONFLICT (request_id) DO NOTHING, so the mutation commits if and only if the outbox row was freshly recorded (transactional outbox: the outcome is atomic with the charge). A client-supplied id that already has a committed outcome is caught by a pre-check and rejected with the new stable code elevator-duplicate-request (409) plus the authoritative state, emitting NO new outcome, so exactly one outcome exists per request. New module src/server/elevator-outbox.ts owns everything outside the transaction: deliverElevatorOutcome emits the structured monitoring event then marks the row delivered (emit-then-mark, so delivery is at-least-once and never loses an outcome; each line carries the requestId for downstream dedup), and drainPendingElevatorOutcomes redelivers stranded rows (committed but undelivered, e.g. a crash between commit and delivery) older than a 30s grace, bounded to 20 per pass. The project has no cron, so the drain runs opportunistically on request traffic (best-effort, never blocking a buy). Every outbox helper swallows its own errors: a sink outage or DB hiccup on delivery can never fail or roll back a committed buy. The success-only elevator.upgrade balance event is untouched (a reject still emits no balance event).
Verification
dash clean, git diff --check clean, biome ci . exit 0 (the 2 pre-existing useOptionalChain warnings are in untouched mine-input-cadence.ts), type-check green, next build green, sim purity green. New outbox unit tests (10): UUID validation accepts/rejects, elevatorOutcomeExists true/false, delivery emits-then-marks and swallows a throwing sink (no mark) and a failed mark, the drain delivers nothing on an empty outbox, redelivers a batch with every id and marks them, and swallows a query error as zero. New monitoring test: the accepted line carries the request id, and omits it on a best-effort emit. New route tests (5, a durable outbox and dedup block): the outbox INSERT rides inside the same statement as the player write and carries the client id; a replayed id is deduplicated with no second charge, no balance event, and no new outcome; a stranded outcome is redelivered by the recovery drain; a failed delivery mark still returns the committed buy; and a legacy client (no id) mints a server-side id and skips the pre-check. Updated: the accepted-outcome assertions now include the requestId, and the api-client and mine-store body assertions include it. Full unit suite green (1655).
Assumptions
Delivery to the log sink is at-least-once (emit-then-mark), not exactly-once: a crash between emit and mark re-emits later, so every emitted line carries the requestId as the downstream dedup key, while the DURABLE record is exactly-once (the unique request_id). Only COMMITTED (accepted) mutations get a durable outbox row, because the transactional-outbox invariant ties the outcome to a committed transaction; rejects commit nothing and keep the existing best-effort log. A truly-concurrent double-submit of the SAME id (both requests past the pre-check in the overlap window) is resolved by the guarded write's FOR UPDATE serialization: the loser's expectedDepth no longer matches, so it classifies as elevator-stale-rail-state (safe: no second charge, client refetches) rather than elevator-duplicate-request; only a SEQUENTIAL replay gets the precise duplicate reason. The opportunistic drain (no cron) delivers stranded outcomes as long as elevator traffic continues; a dedicated cron could call drainPendingElevatorOutcomes later without changing the contract.

Changed
Advances the F-121 "reload-durable / Start-fresh recovery persistence" item. PR #239 shipped the railResyncFailed block (a store gate that disables the rail buy after a conflict resync fails offline) but only IN SESSION: a page reload re-init the flag to false, so an offline reload silently re-enabled a buy against the known-stale local rail. The store persists it at every point it sets railResyncFailed: the buyElevator conflict path writes the block up front, BEFORE the refresh, then re-writes !synced after it, and an accepted buy plus a successful retryRailResync clear it. Writing up front is load-bearing: resyncCloudWorld drops the local trip before its own world fetch, so a reload or crash during that async window would otherwise leave no local trip and no marker; the up-front write is the only thing that survives such a mid-refresh interruption. The reload durability threads through loadWorld, the one place the #239 slice deliberately left it out: on a fresh authoritative load (/api/mine/world ok) the block is cleared in memory and storage (the stale-rail concern is resolved by adopting server truth); on ANY offline load it is RESTORED from storage regardless of whether the local trip survived (the conflict refresh deletes the local trip before its world fetch, so on the real reload path saved is null and the marker is the only thing that keeps the buy gated; a resumed possibly-stale trip is gated too); a dropped corrupt checkpoint clears it (no stale trip remains, clean fresh start). So the gate self-heals the instant an online load reconciles and persists only while a stale local rail actually persists. No new UI: the existing recovery box and the buyElevator authority-boundary guard already render off railResyncFailed, so a restored block shows the Retry affordance and refuses blind buys exactly as in session.

Scope and declines
Three further review points were considered and are documented rather than expanded into this slice. (1) Captured-slot / offline slot hydration: the marker is keyed by activeSlot, the SAME slot the trip blob uses, and is read alongside it, so the two are always paired. On a cold offline mount before loadSaveSlots resolves the real slot, the whole session (mine, trip, marker) is coherently the default slot until an authoritative load re-syncs all of them together, so the marker is never more wrong than the existing trip persistence, and the server expectedDepth guard is the correctness backstop if a buy fires against a pre-hydration slot (it rejects a depth mismatch with no charge). This is a pre-existing slot-keyed-persistence characteristic, not introduced here. (2) In-memory concurrency gate: store actions are serialized on the single-threaded event loop; buyElevator early-returns while railResyncFailed is set (the authority-boundary guard), the marker is written synchronously to localStorage before every await so an interrupted async op is left fail-closed, and the UI's railRetryPending flag prevents a double Retry; a concurrent refetch would in any case be the same idempotent resyncCloudWorld, so no additional in-memory lock is warranted. A third pass rejected the earlier "scope declines" as technically invalid, correctly, and all four are now FIXED rather than argued. (3) activeSlot drift: loadWorld can replace activeSlot from the server across the await, so the marker could be written for a different slot than the conflict. Fixed: the conflict and retry paths capture the slot ONCE and use it for every marker write. (4) Malformed successful responses: a 200 is not authority if malformed, so loadWorld now requires a finite numeric seed (else it falls through to the fail-closed offline branch), loadGear requires both the gear and consumables objects present, and the signed-in checkpoint step requires an explicit { cleared: true } (the route returns 200 { cleared: false } when no player resolves) before the chain counts as full authority. Log every elevator rail write as an accepted or rejected outcome

Branch

PR
No package bump: server-only observability, no player-facing rule change, so no release note and (Rule 13) the mine tips were reviewed with nothing to change; (Rule 14) no stamp (diagnostics are explicitly excluded from stamps).
Changed
Closes the F-121 "Monitoring update" item that adds a structured mutation outcome separate from the success-only elevator.upgrade balance event (the earlier of the two monitoring items; the durable-dedup outbox one below stays open). Before this, the elevator route only recorded the elevator.upgrade balance event on a committed extend, so a rejected write left no structured signal and an operator could not tell an expected concurrency loss from a persistence failure. A new wrapper logElevatorOutcomeEvent in src/server/monitoring.ts emits, through the existing writeMonitoringLog path, a structured log under component elevator.upgrade with event elevator.upgrade.accepted / elevator.upgrade.rejected, a fixed operation (the new exported ElevatorMutation union: place | extend | relocate), a fixed result, and, on a reject, the server-derived low-cardinality ElevatorReasonCode (accepts omit reason). The player id is hashed like every other monitoring wrapper; no human text, world diff, coordinate, or request payload is a reason. Accepts log at info, rejects at warn (an expected stale-client or concurrency guard, distinguishable from a persistence error without alarming). The route (src/app/api/elevator/upgrade/route.ts) resolves the operation once from the loaded profile (placementRequired ? "relocate" : depth === 0 ? "place" : "extend"), reusing the single placementRequired computation the placement branch already needed (the duplicate later computation was removed). One emitOutcome(result, reason) closure, wrapped in try/catch so it can never fail a rail buy, feeds a rejectOutcome wrapper used at every mutation-level reject and two emitOutcome("accepted", null) calls before the relocate and extend success responses, so exactly one outcome fires per mutation-level request. Pre-auth validation rejects (bad content type, malformed body, out-of-range column, missing or out-of-range expectedDepth) stay untouched: they are rejected before the player and profile load, so there is no operation to attribute an outcome to. The success-only elevator.upgrade balance event is unchanged and still fires only on a committed buy, so a rejected write emits this outcome log and no balance event.
Verification
dash clean, git diff --check clean, Biome clean, type-check green. New monitoring unit tests: an accepted outcome writes info JSON with the hashed player and no reason key; a rejected outcome writes warn JSON carrying the reason code; the player field is omitted when no id is supplied. New route tests (a dedicated mutation-outcome telemetry block): an accepted first rail logs one place/accepted/null outcome, an extend logs one extend/accepted, a free placement logs one relocate/accepted, a conflict reject logs one extend/rejected with the classified reason and no balance event, the stale-rail guard logs one extend/rejected before any UPDATE players runs, a pre-auth missing-expectedDepth reject logs no outcome at all, and a throwing telemetry sink still returns a 200 buy. Server + elevator suites green (218); full monitoring and route suites green.
Assumptions
The correct sink is the structured monitoring log (@/server/monitoring), not recordBalanceEvent: the balance event is durable economy telemetry that must stay success-only (no balance event for a rejected write), while the outcome is observability that must fire on rejects too, so they are deliberately separate sinks. operation reflects the request's intent from the pre-write profile (a relocate that loses its race is still an attempted relocate), with reason carrying why it was rejected. The outcome is best-effort: every emission is wrapped so a monitoring failure can never roll back or fail a committed rail buy.

No package bump: a server-side guard hardening plus a client type-tightening, no player-facing rule change for current clients (they already send it), so no release note and (Rule 13) the mine tips were reviewed with nothing to change; (Rule 14) no stamp.
Changed
Closes the F-121 "make expectedDepth required with a stable fail-fast 400 so a stale client cannot bypass the guard" item. expectedDepth is the stale-rail guard: the route compares the client's expected rail depth to the stored depth and rejects a mismatch before any charge, which is what stops a stale or replayed buy (a retry after a lost success response) from silently advancing a second row. It was previously OPTIONAL (the check was if (expectedDepth !== undefined && expectedDepth !== depth)), so a request that simply omitted the field bypassed the guard entirely. It was kept optional only for backward compatibility while clients rolled it out; the store has always sent it (buyRemoteElevator(column, get().gear.elevator) passes the live rail depth, 0 for the first rail), so the only requests without it are stale cached clients, which are exactly what the guard exists to reject. The route (src/app/api/elevator/upgrade/route.ts) now rejects a missing expectedDepth FAIL-FAST, before getOrCreatePlayerId, the DB read, or any charge, with a new stable low-cardinality code elevator-expected-depth-required (added to ELEVATOR_REASON_CODES in src/lib/api-codes.ts) at 400. The downstream stale check simplifies to expectedDepth !== depth now that presence is guaranteed. The client contract is tightened end-to-end: buyRemoteElevator's signature (src/state/mine-api-client.ts) makes expectedDepth required (column: number | undefined, expectedDepth: number) and always includes it in the payload, INCLUDING 0 for the first rail (a plain object spread rather than a falsy-guarded assignment, so depth 0 is never dropped), so a future caller cannot silently omit it and re-open the bypass. The only production caller already passed it, so no call-site change was needed.

New route test: a POST that omits expectedDepth returns 400 elevator-expected-depth-required with "expectedDepth is required" BEFORE any player lookup, DB call, or telemetry (asserts getOrCreatePlayerId, db, and recordBalanceEvent are never called). New client-builder assertion: the payload always carries expectedDepth, including 0 for the first rail. The route test helper's expectedDepth now defaults to the suite's dominant depth-4 rail so a plain request() stays non-stale, while the first-rail (depth 0), maxed (depth 999), and stale-mismatch tests pass their own explicit depth, and the new missing-field test passes null to omit it. Full unit suite green (1604).
Assumptions
Requiring expectedDepth is safe because every current client sends it, so no legitimate live request is rejected; a genuinely stale cached client (from before the field existed) now gets a clear 400 and refreshes to the current client rather than silently buying a second row against a bypassed guard, which is strictly better than the prior silent bypass. fix/rail-resync-blocking-recovery.
PR
No package bump: like the sibling resync fixes (#234, #237) this is client-side error-handling of an existing flow, not a new player-facing rule, so no release note and (Rule 13) the mine tips were reviewed with nothing to change; (Rule 14) no stamp (an error-recovery affordance, not a milestone).
Changed
Closes the F-121 "persistent blocking recovery UI after a failed resync" item. When an elevator rail buy hits a conflict code (elevator-stale-rail-state, elevator-stale-checkpoint, or elevator-concurrent-loss) the client runs one bounded authoritative refetch (resyncCloudWorld). If that refetch itself fails (offline mid-conflict), the local rail state is known-stale and could not be reconciled, yet the old code only set a dismissible shopNote ("couldn't refresh the rail; reopen the shop") and left the rail-buy control live. The store (src/state/mine-store.ts) now carries a distinct railResyncFailed flag (a gate on an action, deliberately not derived from the transient note string): the buyElevator conflict path sets it to !synced, and it is cleared on a successful refresh and on any accepted buy (both the surface-only and post-bank success set blocks). A new retryRailResync action re-runs the same bounded resyncCloudWorld, clears the flag and notes success when the refresh lands, keeps the block (re-noting the failure) when it fails again, and is a no-op when nothing is blocked so it cannot fire a spurious refetch. In the elevator stall menu (src/components/mine-stall-menu.tsx) the rail-buy button is disabled while blocked and a role="alert" recovery box appears with a native "Retry refresh" button wired to retryRailResync through mine-panel.tsx. The retry button uses its own railRetryPending flag rather than the shared elevatorPurchasePending, so the disabled buy button never mislabels as "Buying..." during a refresh; the two controls are mutually exclusive by railResyncFailed (buy blocked while the box is up, box hidden otherwise), so a dedicated flag loses no serialization. One consistent rule (Rule 7): block only the rail-buy action, never trap the player (the shop still closes, mining continues), and the Retry affordance is always offered while blocked so recovery is self-healing once connectivity returns. The note copy changed from "reopen the shop" to "tap Retry to refresh" to point at the new affordance.
Verification
dash clean, git diff --check clean, Biome clean, type-check green. New store tests: a failed post-conflict refresh raises railResyncFailed and the "tap Retry to refresh" note; retryRailResync reconciles world/gear/tripIndex and clears the flag on success; it keeps the block and notes the failure when the refresh fails again; it is a no-op (no fetch) when nothing is blocked; and a successful refresh from the conflict path leaves the flag clear. The two pre-existing failed-resync tests were updated to the new copy and now also assert the flag is raised. The stall-menu render test (refactored to a shared base-props helper, which also removes the prior duplication) asserts the recovery box renders with an enabled retry and the buy control disabled while blocked, and that neither appears in the normal state. Full unit suite green.
Assumptions
The flag is scoped to the buy/retry flow that owns it, the only two resyncCloudWorld callers; it is not threaded into loadWorld or the peer save-sync path. A rare reload that refreshes the world by another route while the flag is set would leave the block up, but the Retry affordance is always offered and a single tap against the already-fresh world clears it, so the block is self-healing rather than stuck. Widening the flag into the hot loadWorld path for that edge would be speculative (slice-discipline) and was declined.

No row change: client error-handling on the already-done elevator transport requirement (REQ-028, the persistent premium rail). The mine store and stall menu are already the refs.

Review round (2026-07-16)
Appended (the entries above are the original committed bytes; the append-only ledger rule keeps corrections additive). Three review-round changes landed. (1) Authority-boundary gate: buyElevator itself now early-returns ("refresh the rail before buying") while railResyncFailed is set, so every caller is blocked, the extend path AND the first-rail placement / relocation path (placeElevatorAtCurrentColumn, reachable from the placement overlay, keyboard, and gamepad, all routing through buyElevator and each able to set the flag on a failed placement resync), not just the stall button. This closes a review-caught bypass where the placement overlay stayed callable for a blind buy and could race Retry. New test: both buyElevator() and buyElevator(column) refuse to hit /api/elevator/upgrade while blocked; beforeEach resets the flag so the store gate cannot leak between tests. (2) Slot-switch clear, fail-closed: switchSaveSlot clears the flag only after BOTH loadWorld() and loadGear() return success, so a switch whose reads fail stays blocked (unconfirmed authority) instead of fail-opening an unblocked buy; the earlier version cleared before awaiting the reads. Tests cover both the confirmed-fresh clear and the failed-read keep. The flag stays a single boolean rather than a per-slot map because a switch reloads the target slot's authority, so "blocked" always means the active slot's rail is unconfirmed; a per-slot pin was considered and declined as over-engineering for state a switch inherently reconciles. (3) Reload-claim correction (superseding the Assumptions note above, which overstated it): the block is in-memory session state and does NOT survive a full page reload. A reload re-inits the store (flag false) and re-runs loadWorld, which loads fresh authority when online but, when offline, resumes the last local trip and returns false, so an offline reload restores possibly-stale local state with no block. That is acceptable because the block is defense-in-depth, not the durable guard: a stale buy is still caught by the server's expectedDepth check plus the conflict resync (unchanged), and an offline buy cannot mutate anyway (the write fetch fails). Review demands that go beyond the blocking-recovery-UI item were considered and NOT adopted here, staying with the separate open F-121 authority/outcome work: a "Start fresh" recovery alongside Retry and a typed-complete-snapshot rewrite of the existing delete-then-load resyncCloudWorld (that resync is the reviewed behavior shipped in #234); a per-slot recovery map; and treating transport-unknown ({ok:false,status:null}) or malformed-200 buy responses as uncertain-committed outcomes that enter the block (the server expectedDepth guard plus conflict resync already prevent a bad mutation after a lost-after-commit response, and this belongs with the uncertain-outcome reconciliation that rides on the request-id / durable-dedup item). The confirmed-reads switchSaveSlot flag clear was REMOVED as dead code: the only caller, the save-slots popup (mine-save-slots-popup.tsx), runs window.location.assign("/mine") on a successful switch, a full page navigation, so no in-memory flag state survives a switch and the target slot boots fresh with its own loadWorld. There is no live cross-slot session in which a stale block could drift, so switchSaveSlot needs no railResyncFailed handling at all and both slot-switch unit tests were dropped. The block therefore reduces to exactly: in-memory session state, gated at the buyElevator authority boundary, cleared by Retry or an accepted buy, and naturally reset by any page reload (including a slot switch) which reloads fresh authority. Appended to calibrate the closure claim honestly (superseding the "Completes ... item" / "DONE" wording in the entries above). What this slice actually ships is the IN-SESSION blocking-recovery UI: a store-level railResyncFailed block that gates every buyElevator caller after a decoded conflict resync fails, plus a Retry affordance, replacing the dismissible reopen note. It is session-only (in-memory): it does NOT persist across a page reload, adds no Start fresh path, is not per-slot, and enters only for the three decoded conflict codes. "none" and a proposed missing/mismatch split were both dead branches and are collapsed to the single bounded reason. The success-only elevator.upgrade economy signal (fromDepth, toDepth, price, refunds, balanceAfter) is otherwise unchanged, and the mine.cash_out event's moves field is the bounded move COUNT (TripResult.moves: number), not a raw action log, so it needs no change. No other telemetry sink retains the column: the reject responses that carry elevatorColumn are the client's own rail state in a response body, not stored telemetry.

The exact shaft column, the only coordinate the item targets, is removed from all three sinks and pinned by serialized-event tests.

Adopt the full authoritative inventory on an elevator buy

Branch
fix/elevator-authoritative-inventory.
PR
#237. No package bump: like the sibling resync fix (#234) this is a server-plus-client correctness hardening of an existing flow, not a new player-facing rule, so no release note and (Rule 13) the mine tips were reviewed with nothing to change; (Rule 14) no stamp (a robustness fix, not a milestone).
Changed
Closes the headline still-open F-121 correctness item: the elevator rail buy (/api/elevator/upgrade) returned only the rail bundle (balance, rail depth, shaft column, ladders, planks, trip index), so the client rebuilt its gear from the LOCAL spread plus the new elevator value and its consumables from LOCAL stock plus the returned supports. A concurrent player-only purchase (a gear upgrade or a consumable buy that leaves the rail depth and world checkpoint untouched) could therefore persist a stale non-rail gear or consumable count under the newly advanced trip. The route now returns the full authoritative gear and consumables (the same shape /api/gear returns) on every accepted buy and on every reject, and the client adopts them wholesale. On the server the two accepted-buy CTEs (first-rail placement/relocation and the extend path) add the non-rail gear and consumable columns to their player_update ... RETURNING and project the row with player_update.*, so the response inventory is the EXACT committed row read atomically inside the guarded write, never a follow-up SELECT that a later concurrent write could shift; a shared inventoryFromRow maps that row through the existing mineGearFromProfile/mineConsumablesFromProfile (whose parameter types were narrowed to MineGearRow/MineConsumablesRow Picks so a route that reads only the inventory columns can map them without the full profile). Every reject carries the same inventory: elevatorStateFromProfile fills it from the pre-write profile and reloadElevatorState's post-conflict re-read now selects the full column set, so the shared ElevatorState bundle (spread into every 409) includes the authoritative gear and consumables. On the client (buyElevator in src/state/mine-store.ts) the response inventory is parsed as ONE atomic, strictly validated unit (authoritativeInventoryFromResponse): every gear level must be a present integer at its floor and the shaft column an integer or null (so normalizeGear cannot turn a garbage or partial body into a plausible level-1 snapshot), every consumable count a present non-negative integer (a negative or fractional count is rejected, not the earlier finite-only guard), AND the fields the response duplicates as top-level scalars (rail depth, shaft column, ladder and plank counts) must equal their nested values, since both come from the same committed row. Any omission, malformed value, or nested/top-level mismatch returns null, so the client adopts NOTHING from a partial or corrupt body: the accepted path then still adopts the valid top-level rail scalars (rail depth, column, balance, trip index, which are the authority-critical fields) and keeps its last-known-good non-rail inventory via the prior rail-only merge, and a reject stays balance-only, rather than persisting mixed authority. That non-rail staleness is reconciled by the server on the next fresh-trip gear load (with an empty log) or on the authoritative cash-out, which recomputes from the player row (a mid-trip loadGear only refreshes top-level gear, so the reconciliation is not guaranteed on the immediate next load). Crucially this fallback path is unreachable with the current server, which always returns a complete, valid, coherent inventory (proven by the route tests); it exists only to keep a buy working against an older server that omits the objects or a corrupted response, where surfacing the valid authoritative rail result beats blocking the UI after a committed spend. When the inventory validates, the accepted path adopts the authoritative gear (keeping the already-validated elevator depth and shaft column) and consumables in place of the local snapshot before the usual surface-trip rebuild and persist; a genuinely older server that omits the objects entirely takes the same rail-only merge (which already adopts the returned support counts). The insufficient-balance and rail-at-bottom rejects, which move nothing server-side, now also adopt the inventory: because rewriting gear/consumables without rebuilding the live mine would desync the store from the sim (the exact corruption the resync slice guarded against), the adoption rebuilds the surface trip over the UNCHANGED world (same tripBaseDiff, replay the surface-only log) and persists, which is replay-identical since buyElevator runs at the surface with a surface-only log; the adopted rail depth equals the local one for both codes (the classifier proves the depth and checkpoint are in sync, else it is a stale-rail or stale-checkpoint conflict that routes through the full resyncCloudWorld refetch instead), so no rail desync is possible. The conflict-code rejects are unaffected: they still run the bounded authoritative refetch, which supersedes the inventory in the body. This returns the player only their own inventory to their own client, so it adds no telemetry surface (the separate elevator.upgrade balance event and its field-scrubbing item are untouched).
Verification
dash clean, git diff --check clean, Biome clean, type-check green. New route tests assert an accepted extend AND a first-rail placement each return the full committed inventory (a concurrently raised gear level and consumable count surface in gear/consumables, with the rail fields consistent), an insufficient-balance reject returns the fresh inventory from the re-read, and (pinning the projection so the mock cannot mask a regression) that the UPDATE players query text actually selects every non-rail inventory column in its RETURNING and projects player_update.*. New store tests prove the client adopts the authoritative gear and consumables on an accepted extend (top-level and mine.gear agree, the persisted trip carries the new counts) and on an insufficient-balance reject (adopted inventory, rebuilt mine, no world refetch, rail depth unchanged), and that a malformed accepted body (a negative gear level), a nested/top-level rail mismatch, and a malformed reject body each adopt NOTHING from the inventory (last-known-good gear and consumables kept, only the valid top-level rail scalars and balance applied); the existing non-stale-reject test still passes on the balance-only fallback for an inventory-less body. Full unit suite green (1593). CI per exact head is recorded in the PR checks. Review: a first exact-head review round asked for strict response validation, atomic parsing with a nested/top-level coherence guard, and the projection-pinning tests; those are addressed here. The same review's broader demands (removing the older-server compatibility fallback and entering a persistent blocked-reconciliation state on any invalid body, overlapping the separately claimed PR #236) were considered and NOT adopted: on a committed success the money is already spent and the rail already extended, so surfacing the valid authoritative rail result and keeping last-known-good non-rail inventory (self-healing on the next gear load) is safer than blocking the UI, and keeping the fallback preserves buys across a client/server deploy skew. That choice is documented rather than silently overridden.
Assumptions
At elevator-buy time the server's consumable counts are the trip-start-equivalent snapshot the client can adopt directly: buyElevator runs at the surface after banking any non-surface log, consumable and gear purchases sync to the server immediately, and the local bought buffer is always empty, so there is no locally-bought-unsynced stock that a wholesale adoption could drop. The accepted response's committed row is read inside the guarded write, so its inventory is coherent with the balance and rail fields the same row returns; the reject re-read is a single SELECT, so its inventory is coherent with the balance it reports. Reading a strictly newer authoritative value than the client held is always an improvement, never a regression, since the client had no better source.
GDD coverage
No row change: this hardens the already-done elevator rail economy (REQ-020) rather than adding coverage. src/app/api/elevator/upgrade/route.ts and its test are already the elevator refs.
Followups
Marks the two headline F-121 inventory items done (adopting the full authoritative player inventory on a committed buy, and on an insufficient-balance reject) and records the remainder still open: making expectedDepth required with a stable 400 (kept optional pending a maintainer policy call); a persistent blocking recovery UI (not just a reopen note) after a failed resync; a request id with durable, deduplicated structured mutation-outcome telemetry (transactional outbox, exactly-once per request); the telemetry field-scrubbing pass; and an integration test exercising a real concurrent spend or bank race.

#235. Package 0.1.273.
Changed
A first-person spawn bug from an Android playtest. The whole bunker volume starts as solid claim rock and only the dug set (including the pre-mined 3x3x3 spawn pocket at floor centre) is open, but fpSpawnCell placed the player at the miner's entry column on the front plane. The rig always plants the feet on the floor (local y 0, z 0), so any entry column outside the 3-wide pocket dropped the player embedded in undug rock, with only a "boxed in" HUD flag and no relocation (they had to walk out to see anything). fpSpawnCell now selects against the built collision grid (the same FpSolidGrid the movement model reads), which stamps BOTH undug rock AND placed parts, and returns the STANDABLE floor-front cell nearest the entry column, scanning outward. This also closes the review's normal-entry case: a part walled onto the entry column is a blocker even though its cell is dug open, so a built-out base no longer spawns the player inside a wall. If the whole front floor row is walled off, the spawn takes any standable cell in the volume (scored so the lowest, nearest-to-front, nearest-to-entry one wins) rather than trusting a centre that could itself be blocked, and only falls back to the footprint centre when nothing is open at all (which the preserved pocket rules out). Because that fallback can pick a cell above the floor, the rig call site now applies the selected cell's y to the feet position (py = y - 0.5) and the occupied-cell index instead of hardcoding the floor row (the third review round caught that an upper-cell result was otherwise ignored, leaving the player in the blocked floor cell). So the player always materializes standing in open space while staying as close to where they entered as the dug, unbuilt room allows. Rule 13 tip review: the "fresh claim is a small pre-mined room" tip is now reliably true from where you actually land; no tip text changed. Rule 14 stamp review: a bug fix, no new mechanic or milestone, no stamp.
Changed (ore, no code)
The same playtest also reported the bunker ore looking low. Investigated and left the generation unchanged. An arbitrary-seed aggregate measurement established the EXPECTED distribution only: bunker ore density tracks the surface mine per row, and each of the five bunker rows samples its OWN mine depth (floor deepest), so deeper rows carry fewer but richer ore cells, never a single row's rate. That is a distribution check, not a reproduction of this player's live seed, footprint, or full z-depth request, and this slice makes no "generation verified correct for the reported bunker" claim; authoritative reproduction and phone legibility stay with the F-116/F-169 ore work. The all-dirt render happens only when a bunker's blockSeed is undefined on the client (bunkerCellBlock is skipped, so no ore or rock is drawn); the server backfill shipped in PR #233 fills that seed on loadBunkerView, which every bunker server op (load, reset, start-fresh, every mutation) returns, so a fresh load already carries it. An earlier draft of this slice added a client-side deriveBunkerBlockSeed fallback in the renderer; that was removed after review because the server credits no ore when the stored seed is genuinely absent (a missing mine seed), so synthesizing a seed only in the renderer could show a vein the server would not pay. The render must reflect the server's authoritative seed, not a client-invented one.

The rig grounds the player on the floor regardless of the miner's row, so the spawn only needs a valid open floor-front cell, which the pre-mined pocket guarantees (unioned into the dug set at every load boundary). The pocket is always present in a bunker the client received from the server (withSpawnPocket in parseBunkerState; seeded at claim), so the pocket-centre backstop is genuinely open.

Resync a rejected rail buy from authoritative state instead of a stale 409

Branch
fix/elevator-upgrade-resync.
PR
#TBD. No package bump: this is a server-plus-client correctness fix to an existing flow, not a new player-facing rule, so no release note and (Rule 13) the mine tips were reviewed with nothing to change; (Rule 14) no stamp (a robustness fix, not a milestone).
Changed
The elevator rail buy (/api/elevator/upgrade) folded insufficient balance, a stale or already-applied rail, and a lost checkpoint race into one prose 409, not enough vibes (or already extended). The client only copied that text into shopNote: it never learned which conflict happened, so the screen could stay confusing after a correct rejection, and because the request omitted the client's expected depth a delayed or retried buy could silently charge for the next row. This slice ships the server classification and the safe client-facing part of F-121. The request now carries expectedDepth (the client's current rail depth); the route rejects a mismatch before any charge, which also makes a retry after a lost success response fail as stale (the committed buy already advanced the depth) rather than buying a second row. Every rejected buy now returns a stable low-cardinality code from ELEVATOR_REASON_CODES in src/lib/api-codes.ts (elevator-insufficient-balance, elevator-stale-rail-state, elevator-stale-checkpoint, elevator-rail-at-bottom, elevator-mine-world-missing, elevator-column-required, elevator-concurrent-loss) plus the authoritative rail bundle (balance, rail depth, shaft column, ladders, planks, trip index, placement-required). When a guarded write matches zero rows the route re-reads and classifies the true cause most-specific-first (moved rail, then column, then moved checkpoint, then balance, else a bare lost race). The checkpoint check comes before balance on purpose: a concurrent spend can both advance the trip and drain the balance below the price, and a moved checkpoint means the whole world advanced under the client, so it must win and drive a refresh rather than report a dead-end price note over a stale rail (the true balance rides back with the refresh). On the client (buyElevator in src/state/mine-store.ts) the reject splits by cause. A conflict reject (elevator-stale-rail-state, elevator-stale-checkpoint, OR elevator-concurrent-loss, the last being a bare lost guarded race, an unknown winner) means another request already moved the world, so all three run one bounded authoritative refetch, resyncCloudWorld. That helper deliberately does NOT reuse the general refreshCloudWorld path: refreshCloudWorld first restores the /api/account/trip checkpoint, which is guarded by seed plus trip count (not rail depth), so a concurrent rail winner can leave the same tripIndex while that payload still carries stale rail gear and moves; restoring it would let loadWorld replay a mixed checkpoint whose gear disagrees with the authoritative rail (a hazard caught in the second review round). resyncCloudWorld instead drops the local trip, then rebuilds world and gear fresh over the authoritative diff (loadWorld's no-local-trip branch zeroes moves on success, so the resync does not pre-clear them and cannot tear a coherent mine/moves pair on a failed read), and loadWorld/loadGear now return an explicit success boolean so the note only claims "refreshed to the latest" when both reads land: a failed fetch fails fast into a "couldn't refresh the rail; reopen the shop" prompt rather than a false success over stale controls. If only the gear read fails after the world rebuilt, the resync drops the local trip again so no new-world/old-gear checkpoint can persist (that checkpoint has no moves, which loadWorld's resume already ignores, but it is dropped regardless). Then, for a signed-in player, it awaits an explicit DELETE of the remote /api/account/trip checkpoint and treats a failed clear as a resync failure (a later refreshCloudWorld downloads that checkpoint BEFORE loadWorld, so a surviving same-tripIndex pre-conflict checkpoint would otherwise be resurrected); guests never wrote such a checkpoint, so they skip it. buyElevator already banks any non-surface log before the request, so dropping the surface-only trip loses nothing. Every remaining code (insufficient balance, or the rail already at the bottom) does not move the world checkpoint: insufficient balance is a guarded-write loss on the price gate with tripIndex confirmed in sync (else it classified as stale-checkpoint above), so the local trip stays valid and only the display-safe balance and a per-code note update; the reject deliberately does not rewrite the top-level gear/tripIndex and persist, which would desync the saved trip from its world (a corruption when the checkpoint moved, found in review and fixed before merge). A concurrent player-only purchase can still leave consumables or gear briefly stale at this same tripIndex; that inventory lag syncs on the next gear load and is the still-open F-121 "authoritative inventory on every reject" item, not a world desync (the third review round flagged the earlier "changed nothing server-side" wording as overclaiming, corrected here). The accepted (success) path rebuilds and persists the whole trip, so it now adopts the response's authoritative ladders/planks instead of adding the refund to local stock (F-121 monitoring item), which stops a lost-success retry or a concurrent inventory change from double-counting supports; older servers that omit the counts still fall back to the local merge. It does NOT yet adopt the full authoritative player inventory (it rebuilds gear from the local spread plus the new elevator value), so a concurrent player-only purchase that leaves elevator depth and tripIndex unchanged can persist a stale non-elevator field under the advanced tripIndex; that is a tracked release-blocking F-121 item (the route would need to return full gear and consumables), not a claim this path is fully authoritative. buyRemoteElevator gained the optional expectedDepth argument.
Verification
dash clean, git diff --check clean, Biome clean, type-check green. New route tests cover each reason code: a stale expectedDepth rejected before any UPDATE players with the authoritative state returned, a non-integer expectedDepth rejected 400, an expectedDepth that matches extending normally, a losing guarded write classified from a re-read into insufficient-balance, moved-rail, moved-checkpoint, or concurrent-loss, and a combined moved-checkpoint-plus-low-balance re-read reported as a moved checkpoint (proving the checkpoint check wins over balance). New store tests prove the client sends expectedDepth; that a non-stale reject (insufficient balance over an in-sync checkpoint) fires no world refetch and updates only the balance and coded reason, leaving the rail depth, trip index, and supports untouched with no corrupted trip persisted; that a stale-rail reject runs the bounded world-plus-gear refetch, never fetches /api/account/trip, and leaves top-level gear, mine.gear, moves, trip index, and balance all authoritative (no mixed state); the regression case where the account-trip endpoint holds a same-index stale-rail checkpoint and the resync still ends aligned by ignoring it; that a concurrent-loss reject also refetches; that a failed world read during the resync fails fast into the reopen prompt; that a failed gear read after a successful world rebuild also fails fast and drops the local trip so no mixed checkpoint persists; that a signed-in resync clears the remote /api/account/trip checkpoint (DELETE) so it cannot be resurrected; and that a failed DELETE during a resync fails fast into the reopen prompt rather than reporting success over a surviving stale checkpoint. The accepted path still replaces support stock from the response rather than re-adding the refund. New api-client assertions pin that expectedDepth is sent when present and omitted when not. The tests mock the sql/fetch layer, so they cover the classification, the reject contract, and the refetch chain but not a real concurrent write; an integration test against a real spend or bank race is a follow-up. Full unit suite green after the fix. CI per exact head is recorded in the PR checks.
Assumptions
expectedDepth stays optional so older clients and other callers keep working; when omitted the depth guard is skipped and the prior behavior stands (an old client can still bypass the guard until it updates). The expectedDepth guard gives the double-advance protection F-121 asked a request id for (a committed buy moves the depth, so any stale or replayed buy mismatches and returns the already-advanced depth); this is a stale rejection that reports the truth, not an idempotent replay, and there is no double-charge, so a durable request-id dedup is not needed for spend correctness and is deferred with the telemetry work. The bounded refetch is safe on the reject path because buyElevator runs at the surface and banks any non-surface log first, so the dropped trip carries no unbanked progress. It uses the elevator-specific resyncCloudWorld (skips the seed+tripIndex account-trip restore) rather than refreshCloudWorld, because the account-trip checkpoint can carry stale rail gear at the same tripIndex; refreshCloudWorld is left unchanged for its existing cross-device callers, whose account-trip restore is appropriate there and out of this slice's scope.
GDD coverage
No row change: this hardens the already-done elevator rail economy (REQ-020) rather than adding coverage. src/app/api/elevator/upgrade/route.ts and its test are already the elevator refs.
Followups
Ships the server reason-code classification (moved checkpoint ahead of balance), the expected-depth guard, the account-trip-skipping bounded refetch on every conflict code (moved rail, moved checkpoint, and bare concurrent loss) with explicit success/failure and a fail-fast reopen prompt, the display-safe reject for the non-conflict codes, and the accepted-path authoritative support-count replacement for F-121. A Progress note on F-121 records the remainder still open and NOT marked done: a request id with durable, deduplicated structured mutation-outcome telemetry (transactional outbox, exactly-once per request); the telemetry field-scrubbing pass; and an integration test exercising a real concurrent spend or bank race.

Backfill a block seed so old bunkers stop rendering as barren dirt

Branch
fix/bunker-seedless-ore.
PR
#TBD. Package 0.1.272.
Changed
A player in the first-person bunker builder reported seeing no ore. Root cause: a bunker claimed before block seeds existed (F-116) stores block_seed NULL, which the server reads as an undefined seed; with no seed every undug cell renders as plain dirt and pays nothing when dug, and Start fresh (F-117) never writes the column, so a reset does not fix it. This is the seed-only recovery the user chose ("Just fix the seed") for a row whose layout is already current and whose sole defect is the missing seed; PR #228 tracks the wider fail-fast contract under F-165. loadBunkerView now backfills a seedless bunker: it derives deriveBunkerBlockSeed(mineSeed, footprint) from the player's mine_worlds seed (the exact value a fresh claim assigns) and persists it with a guarded write (UPDATE bunkers SET block_seed = ... WHERE player_id = ... AND block_seed IS NULL RETURNING block_seed). RETURNING reports whether the write landed: a winner returns its stored value; a zero-row loser (a concurrent load already backfilled) re-reads the authoritative seed rather than trusting the local one, so the view is never a synthesized success. The seed is deterministic, so the two always agree, but reading the row keeps the response consistent with the database. A missing or malformed mine seed cannot derive real blocks, so the bunker is returned unchanged (renders as dirt) instead of seeded from a garbage value. The existing exposed-ore rendering then shows the ore and future digs pay it, with no fake overlay and no generation or economy change. Backfilling cannot re-credit already-dug cells (banked digs credit at excavate time and a pending claim is always seeded at claim, so the bulk settleBunkerDig replay never runs on a backfilled row). This supersedes the closed PR #232, which tried to paint ore hints on the walls: those rendered inside the opaque wall block (occluded, so invisible) and decorated non-ore cells (misleading), and did not address the seedless root cause. Rule 13 tip review: the bunker-ore tip already covers walls showing dirt/rock/ore and is now accurate for backfilled bunkers too; no tip changed. Rule 14 stamp review: no new stamp (a data backfill, no new mechanic or milestone).
Verification
dash clean, git diff --check clean, Biome clean, type-check green. Five bunker.test.ts backfill cases: a seedless bunker gains the seed the guarded RETURNING write reports and now generates at least one ore cell; a zero-row race re-reads and adopts the authoritative seed; an already-seeded bunker is untouched with no world lookup or write; a malformed mine seed leaves the bunker unseeded and writes nothing; and a bunker with no mine world likewise stays unseeded. Full unit suite green (1563). The release-note fresh-browser and recent-list e2e are updated for 0.1.272 and pass locally. The required parallel CI gate is verified per exact head in the PR comments.
Assumptions
The backfilled seed matches what a fresh claim would assign for the same footprint, so the client preview and the server payout agree exactly as they do for a freshly claimed bunker; a bunker row always carries a valid footprint (written at claim), so the derivation never sees a null footprint; and the backfill deliberately does not advance the revision or fail visibly, because it changes no edit-relevant state (parts, dug, loot untouched) and self-heals silently, so forcing a client resync would only interrupt an in-flight edit for no gain. Backfilling during an active raid is harmless (the frozen raid snapshot drives the raid from parts and dug, never the block seed, and the settlement write is guarded on the revision the backfill leaves untouched), so it is not blocked. The fuller fail-fast, revision-advancing, telemetry-bearing recovery for other unsupported states stays with PR #228 F-165 under the Q-022 boundary.

Seed-recovery tracking stays with PR #228 F-165 (referenced here rather than duplicated) and the thin-parts remainder stays under REQ-046 / F-117, so this slice adds no new followup id.

Start fresh becomes a guarded compare-and-swap after review

#231 (F-117 slice 3). Correction record for the bunker-layout-version-reset article below, added rather than editing it (append-only).
Changed
Two exact-head review rounds. Round A found a real TOCTOU race the prior article's "idempotent no-op" claim did not cover: startFreshBunker loaded the bunker, checked it incompatible, then ran an unconditional UPDATE by player_id. A request that read a legacy bunker, paused while a concurrent Start fresh reset it and the player rebuilt it to a current layout, then resumed, would wipe the rebuilt state. Round B found that even the guarded write deviated from the established F-122 conflict contract by reporting success on a lost race. Fixed across both: the destructive UPDATE is a guarded compare-and-swap, WHERE player_id = ? No client change: the store already resyncs on that conflict code. Also strengthened the Rule 9 smoke to assert the recovery is a single POST, and returned the version framing to a build-era generation (whole-cell parts are not invalid; resetting version-0 rows is the Q-022 product decision to clear pre-redesign layouts).

Invisible sim slice building on the slot vocabulary: placeBasePart and removeBasePart now take a trailing optional slot and enforce the thin model's structural rules, so a layout can never hold an impossible part. Placement into a slot resolves the canonical wall divider, rejects a slot a part cannot use ("slot"), rejects a second part in a taken slot ("occupied"), keeps a roof only where nothing is open above it ("roof-top"), and requires an overhead floor (open space below) to have at least two supporting walls in the cell beneath it ("unsupported"); a floor resting on the ground needs none. #TBD (package 0.1.268).
Changed
Gave touch players a discoverable way out of a live first-person raid (F-162). F-160 made every exit forfeit correctly, but the in-fight Exit control is hidden during a raid and the only voluntary leave path was the desktop Escape key, so a phone player had no visible way to abandon a raid short of closing the tab. The raid HUD's active branch (bunker-fp-hud.tsx) now renders a confirm-guarded Leave raid control: a Leave raid button arms a two-step confirm (Forfeit / Stay), so a stray tap while fighting only reveals the confirm and cannot cost the raid. Forfeit calls the same onExit handler as Escape, so it exits first person, unmounts BunkerFpCanvas, and forfeits through the F-160 unmount effect (one /api/bunker/raid/forfeit POST, no reward, no wear, no re-roll on re-entry). A small effect resets the armed state whenever the raid ends so it never leaks into the won/lost panel. Styling in mine.css: the raid panel wraps and the abandon controls opt back into pointer events (pointer-events: auto) since the panel itself is pointer-events: none; Forfeit is the destructive fill, Stay is neutral. No server, store, or sim change; this is a HUD affordance over the existing forfeit path.
Verification
dash clean, git diff --check clean, Biome clean, full type-check, full unit suite green (1544 tests). New first-person e2e in mine-bunker-fp.spec.ts, run in a phone context (390x760, hasTouch, isMobile) with real touch tap so it exercises the coarse-pointer path a phone player actually takes: it starts a raid, pauses the R3F render loop at the opening tick (the same wrapped requestAnimationFrame harness as the Escape-forfeit test), checks the Leave raid target is at least 44px tall and fully inside the 390px viewport, taps it, and asserts the confirm appears and that arming alone does not leave (still in first person, zero forfeit POSTs), then backs out with Stay (the confirm collapses, still raiding), re-arms, and confirms Forfeit: exactly one POST to /api/bunker/raid/forfeit, zero to /api/bunker/raid/resolve, first person exited, and no raid on re-entry. The existing live-raid and Escape-forfeit e2es still pass with the panel restyle. Release chain updated for 0.1.268 (app-release unit, notifications route unit, release-notifications e2e) and green.
Assumptions
The abandon control is deliberately a two-step confirm rather than a one-tap bail, matching the Q-019 decision that leaving a raid is a deliberate act (a key, a confirm) and not an inviting always-visible Exit button. It reuses onExit rather than calling the store forfeit directly so there is exactly one forfeit path (the canvas unmount) and no risk of a double settlement; both forfeit and resolve remain idempotent server-side on result IS NULL. Because it runs on the client HUD over the unchanged forfeit route, MINE_VERSION and SIM_VERSION are unchanged.

Diff, dash, Dot, lint, typecheck, and full unit verification are recorded on the additive head.
Assumptions
Cancellation is a local pre-dispatch action, never a network or authoritative-state shortcut. If transport cancellation cannot prove the server did not commit, the request remains logically dispatched and its stable identity plus authoritative response or conflict replacement still controls recovery.

Leaving a live raid forfeits it

Branch
feat/fp-raid-forfeit-on-exit.
PR
#224 (package 0.1.267).
Changed
Closed the leave and re-enter gap in the live first-person raid (F-160). The raid runs client-side and submits one bounded outcome only on a natural win or loss, so leaving first person mid-fight previously left the raid row active (result IS NULL) until the scheduled expiry forfeited it; the client store still held the activeLiveRaid, so re-entering spun up a fresh runtime against the same frozen snapshot and re-rolled the fight. Now leaving forfeits immediately. New server function forfeitLiveRaid (src/server/bunker.ts) settles the active row as {outcome:"forfeit", survived:false} with no reward and no bunker wear, guarded by result IS NULL AND raid_version = BUNKER_RAID_LIVE_VERSION so it is idempotent and can never overwrite a fought outcome, and returns the cleared view. New route /api/bunker/raid/forfeit (src/app/api/bunker/raid/forfeit/route.ts, node runtime) mirrors the finish route through withPlayerRoute/operationResultResponse. Client plumbing: forfeitRemoteLiveRaid (bunker-api-client), a forfeitLiveRaid store action (bunker-store) that adopts the cleared view through the shared monotonic guard, and the forfeit trigger itself on the outer BunkerFpCanvas component: it wraps onResolveRaid to record the resolved raid id and, on unmount, forfeits when the liveRaid prop is still an unresolved raid. mine-panel.tsx wires the store action to the canvas. The interim flat raid and the natural win/loss resolve path are untouched.
Verification
dash clean, git diff --check clean, Biome clean, full type-check. New server-function test in bunker-raid-live-server.test.ts (idempotent no-reward settlement: the row is written once with the forfeit result, no players or bunkers writes, the returned view carries no active raid) and a store test in bunker-store.test.ts (the action adopts the cleared, raid-free view). Full unit suite green. New first-person e2e in mine-bunker-fp.spec.ts: it enters first person, starts a raid, pauses the R3F render loop (a wrapped requestAnimationFrame) once the raid HUD is on screen so the sim holds at its opening tick, then leaves mid-raid the only way a player can (the Exit control is hidden during a fight, so it presses Escape, which the fp exit handler treats as leave-the-view), and asserts exactly one POST to /api/bunker/raid/forfeit and zero to /api/bunker/raid/resolve. It then unfreezes, re-enters, and asserts the raid does not reappear (the flat Start-raid control returns instead). Freezing the loop is required for determinism: a headless runner stutters rAF and processes a catch-up burst on each interaction, and the player spawns at the entry edge, reachable from the un-wallable mine-approach cell in front, so without the freeze the fight resolves on its own and races the forfeit. Release chain updated for 0.1.267 (app-release unit, notifications route unit, release-notifications e2e) and green.
Assumptions
Placing the forfeit on the outer (plain DOM) canvas component, not inside the R3F scene, means its unmount cleanup is an ordinary React teardown that runs reliably when the fp view is torn down, and it keys off the liveRaid prop (still the active raid at unmount, since exiting fp does not clear the store) plus the resolved-raid-id it records when the scene reports a natural win or loss, rather than the scene's runtime ref, so it fires even when the player leaves before the scene's runtime effect has committed and never forfeits a just-settled raid. Forfeit and resolve both guard on result IS NULL, so even a double submission during the resolve-then-exit window is idempotent server-side. This implements the Q-019 expiry-as-forfeit default at leave time; the scheduled finalizeExpiredLiveRaids still catches abandoned tabs that never unmount cleanly. Server and client change only the settlement of an abandoned raid: MINE_VERSION and SIM_VERSION unchanged.
GDD coverage
No requirement status changed (settles an already-specified live raid, REQ-037). Appended a build-log entry to 08-base-building.html. Rule 13: reviewed the mine tip rotation and added one tip (leaving a live raid forfeits it, so you cannot slip out and retry); no stale tip needed removal. Rule 14: stamp review recorded, no new stamp: a forfeit is a rule-tightening loss, not a milestone or new mechanic, and surviving a live raid already earns First Defense and Buttoned Up. The optional live-raid stamp remains F-161.
Followups
Resolves F-160. Raised F-162: the Exit control is hidden during a raid, so on touch (no Escape key) a player has no visible way to abandon a live raid short of closing the tab; decide whether to add a confirm-guarded in-raid Abandon control or to document committing-once as the intended design. Next in the arc: F-118 (retire the spinning core after the interim flat raid is removed) and F-117 (thin rotatable walls plus the staircase part).

F-112. The pending-bunker checkpoint was validated in scattered, unsafe ways: the account trip route accepted pendingBunker as z.unknown(), a shallow client guard only checked that parts was an array, and the hand-rolled normalizer then dereferenced part.depth on every element, so a malformed checkpoint such as parts: [null] threw instead of producing a stable state error. Rejecting the whole trip on an invalid pending bunker (rather than dropping only the bunker) is correct because the trip's move log can reference the claim, so a bunker-less-but-moves-present trip would desync. The recovery notice is scoped to a corrupt pending bunker (not every unrestorable trip) so a routine MINE_VERSION bump does not alarm guests with a reset message. Auto-recovering with a notice beats a blocking Start fresh button (Rule 7: simplest consistent path). The checkpoint schema is deliberately separate from the bank route's flat claim schema, which is a different wire shape and authoritative on its own.

Stop concurrent bunker edits from losing or regressing each other

Branch
fix/bunker-edit-revision-guard.
PR
#202.
Changed
F-122. Banked bunker edits launched remote writes with no in-flight or revision guard: the server read the bunker then unconditionally wrote it, and the store applied responses in arrival order, so a held-strike burst or a delayed reply could lose an excavation or regress the client view. Added optimistic concurrency end to end. The bunkers table gained a revision counter; loadBunkerView returns it and every state-changing write bumps it. The place, remove, move, and excavate server wrappers take an expectedRevision and persist through a guarded UPDATE (WHERE revision = expected, SET revision = revision + 1, RETURNING), so exactly one edit per revision wins; a stale expected revision or a lost race returns HTTP 409 with the stable code bunker-revision-conflict and the authoritative view in the body (a generic failure code/body was threaded through operationResultResponse). The dig CTE keeps the ore payout atomic with the guarded dug write and reports the dug row count so a lost race pays nothing; reset, repair, and raid-start bump the revision too so an in-flight edit cannot clobber them. On the client, the store tracks the revision, echoes it as expectedRevision, and serializes every bunker write through one chain (each queued write reads the freshest revision, so a burst threads incrementing revisions instead of racing): the four banked edits plus buy, collect-loot, and skin, so a non-bumping write can never carry a revision a concurrent edit already advanced past and get dropped. It drops any reply that would move the revision backwards, reports success only for a body it actually adopted, recognizes the conflict body by the shared bunker-revision-conflict code (in src/lib/api-codes.ts), and on a conflict adopts the authoritative view then reports failure so a retry runs against fresh state. Aim retargeting stays local and responsive; pending-claim edits stay on the synchronous local mine-store path, untouched.
Verification
dash, git diff --check, typecheck, Biome, the full unit suite (1,468 tests). New coverage: server guard tests (matching revision wins, stale rejects before any write, concurrent loss 409s, omitted-revision fallback to the loaded value, stale dig rejected before touching the dug set); a route test (the revision threads to the server call, and a 409 conflict serializes the code plus the authoritative view fields); store scenario tests (serialized rapid different-cell edits thread the incrementing revision, an out-of-order reply is dropped, a conflict resyncs to the authoritative view and a retry uses the fresh revision, a duplicate same-cell dig fails without regressing state, placement is serialized and guarded too). The banked first-person dig, place, and pry e2es now assert the expectedRevision in each request body and pass against a fresh production build. The existing bunker server, route, store, and api-client suites pass with their mocks updated to report the guarded writes as won.
Assumptions
One store instance edits one player's bunker, so serializing its banked edits through a single chain is sufficient client-side; the server guard is the cross-tab and cross-device safety net. Bunker cells are single-hit digs, so "reconcile repeat cadence with accepted strike completion" is met by the store serialization (every queued strike lands in order, none overlaps) rather than a per-cell hit counter. Older clients that omit expectedRevision fall back to the loaded revision, which still serializes concurrent writes through the guarded UPDATE, so the rollout needs no client-version gate.
GDD coverage
No requirement status changed and no GDD section file was touched (server and client concurrency hardening, not a design or player-facing change). REQ for base building stays accurate.
Followups
Resolves F-122. Unblocks the remaining F-114 held-swing and F-116 multi-hit work against banked bunkers, which the missing edit guard was blocking.

feat/bunker-block-art.

#198.
Changed
Package 0.1.263 corrects the visual half of F-116. A user report ("the cells in the bunker need to look like the dirt and ores outside") exposed that F-116's claimed per-kind tint never rendered: FpRockInstances built one instanced mesh (dirt-cube geometry + a single rock material) and called setColorAt per instance, but both bunker block materials are MeshStandardNodeMaterial whose color comes from a procedural colorNode, and node materials ignore instanceColor. The whole interior therefore rendered as one flat gray: no rock forms, no ore crystals. The economy was correct throughout (ore yield, banking, depletion all keyed off bunkerCellBlock); only the pixels were dead. FpRockInstances now routes each undug cell by its real block kind into one of two instanced meshes built from the mine's own art (DIRT_BLOCK_GEOMETRY + dirtBlockMaterial(dirtHex) for dirt, ROCK_BLOCK_GEOMETRY + rockBlockMaterial for rock) and renders an OreCrystals overlay (the mine's own component) on exposed ore cells. Because the kinds come from bunkerCellBlock (the shared generatedCell keyed to each cell's real mine row), ore appears at exactly the surface mine's distribution for that depth, not on every cell, matching the user's follow-up ("distributed similarly to the actual ore distribution for that level"). Render-only over unchanged colliders, sim, and economy.

The WIP bumped 54 to 55, but main independently reached 55 (PR #189) without the ore economy, so shipping the economy at 55 would let in-flight pre-ore clients preview a bank total without bunker ore while the server (which seeds a block seed for every fresh claim) banks with it. Smoother movement rendering: held steps chain into one stride

Package 0.1.243, slice two of the movement-feel plan. Motion tracks gain an ease weight: a step that continues the previous one (starts within CHAIN_GAP_SECONDS of its end, heading the same way) becomes a chained segment running the full input-repeat interval (minerChainStepSeconds) with a mostly-linear cruise (CHAIN_EASE_WEIGHT 0.35), so held walks and climbs stride through cell boundaries instead of decelerating to zero and idling ~90ms at every cell. Isolated taps keep the classic soft settle at 86% of the interval. Death playback and trip-reset snap paths are untouched (easeWeight defaults to full ease for externally built tracks). Speed is unchanged: the same one cell per legal action interval, rendered continuously. GDD render-juice clause amended per the approved plan.

Timing stays render/input-side only: the move log is order-only, so replay verification, MINE_VERSION, and SIM_VERSION are untouched.

12 cadence unit tests (buffer at legal time only, no banking, opposite cancel, held-opposite still moves, OS-repeat no trailing step, isAutoRepeat flags), sim predicate tests, three new keyboard e2es (same-tick tap bursts: buffered tap lands once at the legal time; opposite cancels; held-up mines a ceiling without planting a ladder, fresh press plants). Rebuild surface parallax around a fixed celestial plane

Branch
fix/rebuild-surface-parallax.
PR
#157.
Changed
Package 0.1.238 replaces both earlier parallax formulas. Sky, stars, and the ringed planet are camera-space layers with zero translational parallax. Their meshes align inside onBeforeRender from the final camera transform and immediately refresh matrixWorld, so neither the 280 ms camera damping nor callback ordering can produce a one-frame or after-step slide. Only earthbound layers move, using standard linear scroll scales: 0.08 far terrain, 0.18 industry, and 0.32 near berm. The rejected nonlinear curve, travel caps, and independent backdrop frame callback are gone. The berm widens to 163.2 units for full biome coverage, and the fixed planet center moves from 6.6 to 5.2 so its upper-right crop remains intentional on portrait screens. SurfaceDressing stays prop-free and memoized. MINE_VERSION stays 53; SIM_VERSION stays 5.
Verification
Pure tests pin a fixed celestial plane through a representative damped camera trace, monotonic linear terrain rates, consistent response at village and biome extremes, cache reuse, bounds, triangle budgets, and reduced motion. Exact 448x923 DPR 2.25 touch WebGL2 coverage walks from Base +16 to +17, samples every rendered frame through the camera settle, proves zero celestial matrix displacement, and verifies 35,044 planet-colored pixels keep the identical centroid at both endpoints. The final 12-capture motion matrix held 12 to 14 draws; phone median was 8.3 to 8.4 ms and p95 no more than 16.7 ms. The 72-second heap probe measured 2.51 MB/s, 14 collection drops, and a 24.5 MB trough. Full verification is recorded before PR closeout.
Assumptions
Recommended default: celestial distance is treated as infinite for surface-scale translation, so planet parallax is exactly zero. Earthbound layers alone communicate depth. Mine tips reviewed with no copy change because no rule changed. Stamp review completed with none added because this is visual correction.

Stream tunnel floors and darkness veils through the instanced grid: the warp/fall window-jump stall
