Changed
Build 272605 (contains the instanced grid, the warm-up, the constant-light fix, and the DPR cap) was confirmed on the real Pixel across three sessions (2026-07-09/10, eda665, 273174, d6ad6c): light count pinned at 4, heap flat, steady digging and idling clean at 16.8 ms p95 with zero stalls. The residual 0.4-1.7 s (worst 3.7 s) freezes correlated one-for-one with multi-row camY jumps (falls, warps, fast climbs between the surface and row 24) and never occurred while stationary. Cause: cell elements are keyed by absolute col:row, so a teleport-sized window shift replaces every key and React unmounts and remounts the whole window's overlay set in one commit inside rAF; the F-075 cell cache only helps cells that stay on screen (and the over-limit sweep evicts entries one render after they leave, so warp-and-return rebuilds them). Shipped the follow-on lever the instanced-grid slice named: the two high-count overlay classes now ride the block-instance plan. BlockInstance widened its material type to Material (the veil is a MeshBasicMaterial); each class's constant depth offset (floor -0.42, veil 0.72, the old per-mesh position z) is baked into its shared geometry, so the plan carries only cell positions; InstancedBlockGrid gives transparent buckets renderOrder 1 (one instanced draw cannot per-quad depth sort, and the darkness veil's job is to occlude the cell, so it draws after the default transparent pass). The render loop pushes the recessed tunnel floor (empty cells at row 1 and below, one bucket per biome material, biomes resolved once per visible column per pass) and the lamp-edge darkness veil (one bucket per 0.02-quantized opacity material) into the plan; buildCellEntry no longer builds either element, the cell signature drops its darkness term, and the darkness min/max dataset diagnostics are computed in the loop (the e2e data-darkness-opacity-* assertions keep their source). The warm-up compiles both classes' instanced programs at load: the darkness buckets switched to instanced warm meshes in place, and the tunnel floors moved from the plain-mesh warm set (collectBlockNodeMaterials) into the new collectInstancedGridMaterials in mine-material-warmup.ts, which both keeps the variant enumeration in the module that owns it and stops compiling three plain-mesh floor programs at load that nothing draws anymore. Sparse decorations (ladders, planks, beacons, drops, bags, cracks) stay React. No version bump; MINE_VERSION stays at 50; SIM_VERSION stays at 4.

Remove the mine's dynamic point lights: the real cause of the mid-play freezes

Branch
claude/instanced-grid-rewrite-es0i83.
PR
Pending.
Changed
The actual root cause of the residual stalls, pinned from the preview-build telemetry. The instancing, decoration-sharing, and material warm-up slices removed the GC-pause and per-cell-mount classes, but ~0.6 to 1.8 s stalls remained. The session drilldown for build 272557 (which contains the warm-up) settled it: every stall coincides exactly with a change in the scene's light count (5 to 4, 4 to 5, 5 to 6, ...), and whenever the count holds steady the mine runs a locked 16.8 ms. three recompiles every material program in the scene whenever the number of lights changes, so a material warm-up could never touch it (and it reproduces on desktop, ruling out GC and fill). The count fluctuated because the decorative point lights, warp beacons, dropped bags, dynamite fuses, and active surface portals, enter and leave the render window as the miner moves, each toggling the recompile. That is why the lag fired on falls, ladder descents, crush deaths, drops from the surface, and "randomly": all are a light-bearing cell crossing the window edge. Fix: drop those per-cell point lights (beacon in mine-canvas.tsx, dropped bag and dynamite in mine-block-render.tsx, active portal in mine-surface-render.tsx), keeping their emissive meshes (the beacon emissive is bumped 1.6 to 1.9 to stay a landmark). The only point light left is the miner's lamp, which is always present, so the scene's light count is now constant (ambient, hemisphere, directional, lamp) and no move triggers a recompile. No version bump; MINE_VERSION stays at 50; SIM_VERSION stays at 4.
Verification
Diagnosis from real-device telemetry: session 76c778 (build 272557, arm valhall webgl2/low) drilldown shows stalls at seq 2/10/11/12/21/22, each on a lightCount change, and 0 stalls across the 18 steady-count snapshots. Local tsc/vitest/build/Playwright still cannot run here (the egress-blocked @randroids-dojo/vibekit dependency); Biome, em-dash, and git diff --check are clean. This is the cleanest possible confirmation target: after deploy, lightCount should hold constant across a play session and per-session maxFrameMs/stallCount should collapse to the 16.8 ms steady state. CI runs the full gate.
Assumptions
Recommended default: remove the dynamic point lights rather than build a fixed-size point-light pool. Both keep the count constant, but removal is guaranteed correct and cannot introduce a flicker/miscount bug (the pool is unverifiable here), and the emissive meshes preserve most of the look. If the local point-light glow around beacons/dynamite is missed, a fixed-count accent-light pool (always N lights in the scene, reassigned to the nearest emitters) is the follow-on that restores it without reintroducing the recompile. The material warm-up is kept: with the light count now constant, its load-time compile finally matches the play-time program key, so the two are complementary. Rule 13: mine tips reviewed, no change (lights are cosmetic; no mine rule changed). Rule 14: stamp review done, none added.

Pre-compile mine materials at load to kill the first-use shader-compile stall

Branch
claude/instanced-grid-rewrite-es0i83 (follow-on to the decoration-sharing slices below).
PR
Pending.
Changed
Diagnosed from the preview-build real-device telemetry (GET /api/performance/insights?device=real). The instancing and decoration-sharing slices resolved the F-074 GC-pause class: on the newest builds (0.1.203.272496/272515) steady state is a locked ~60 fps, the heap no longer sawtooths, and the old 4.5 s freeze (build 269524, worst p95 4475 ms) is gone (worst p95 16.8 ms). What remained was intermittent ~0.6 to 1.0 s stalls, every one LoAF-attributed to FrameRequestCallback, with the same stalls present on a desktop Apple M-series WebGPU session (766 ms frame, 4004 ms long-frame window) where GC and reconcile are not credible causes. That signature is first-use shader/pipeline compilation: three compiles each material program lazily on its first draw, so a new tint/kind appearing mid-play (a stratum tint, an ore crystal, a rock tier, a shard glow, the darkness overlay) hitches a frame. This slice pre-compiles every mine material once at mine load so the cost is paid behind the load, not per action: a new warmMineMaterials in mine-canvas.tsx builds one tiny offscreen mesh per material and calls renderer.compileAsync in a mount effect. The instanced block bodies (dirt, ore, rock, metal) warm on an InstancedMesh because the instanced draw compiles a distinct program; crystals, tunnel floor, gas, boulder, shards, supports, and the darkness buckets warm on plain meshes. The variant enumeration lives in the new mine-material-warmup.ts (block node materials) plus the shard/support/darkness sets the canvas already owns; the palette now exports its dirt and rock tint arrays for it. Best-effort: if the renderer lacks compileAsync or it throws, materials fall back to lazy compile (today's behavior), so the warm-up can never break the mine. No version bump; MINE_VERSION stays at 50; SIM_VERSION stays at 4.
Verification
Partial in the authoring container (the egress-blocked @randroids-dojo/vibekit dependency prevents tsc/vitest/build/Playwright locally). Ran: Biome clean on all changed files; em-dash and git diff --check clean. Manual review confirmed the warm-up compiles the same programs the game draws (same geometry attribute set, and the instanced program is warmed on an InstancedMesh) and that the shard glow set matches FallingRockShard's discrete glows. This one needs on-device confirmation: after deploy, the newest build's session drilldown should show maxFrameMs and per-session stallCount drop toward the steady-state 16.8 ms, and the desktop long-frame windows shrink. CI runs the full gate.
Assumptions
Recommended default: warm on compileAsync in a post-mount useEffect (not layout) so the first paint is not blocked; the compile burst lands just after mount, behind the mine's load. Warm only the live detail tier (the other tier compiles if the player flips quality, which re-runs the effect). Scoped to the mine render materials; the surface-village and workshop/holodeck materials are out of scope. If telemetry still shows a residual stall, the next suspect is the sim-side tickFalls all-cells scan. Rule 13: mine tips reviewed, no change (render-path perf, no player rule changed). Rule 14: stamp review done, none added.

Imperative instanced block grid: stop the scroll-churn behind the fall and ladder lag (F-075 escalation)

Branch
claude/instanced-grid-rewrite-es0i83.
PR
Pending.
Changed
The user still reports lag when falling, walking down ladders, and at random, after the F-075 cell-signature cache, the DPR cap, and the geometry-sharing leak fix. The cell cache only helps cells that stay on screen; every action that scrolls the window (a step down, and especially a multi-row fall) still mounted a fresh row of block meshes and unmounted the row that left, so React reconciled a scene-graph mount/unmount burst per action, which is the residual churn F-075 named the imperative-instanced-grid escalation for. Shipped that escalation. The static solid bodies (dirt, ore body, non-fallen rock, metal), the dominant on-screen mass, now stream through an imperative InstancedMesh grid instead of one React-reconciled mesh per cell: new src/components/mine-instanced-grid.ts (InstancedBlockGrid, one InstancedMesh per (geometry, shared material) bucket, two-pass matrix streaming with lazy pool creation and doubling growth), new three-free planning core src/components/mine-block-plan.ts (the pooled BlockInstancePlan and the instancedBlockDraw classifier, node-testable), and instancedBlockBody in mine-block-render.tsx as the single source mapping a cell to its geometry/material/rotation (mirrors MineBlockBody exactly). In mine-canvas.tsx the render loop fills the plan for every instanced cell (on cache hit and miss alike, since the plan is not cached) and a layout effect rewrites the instance matrices and counts after each render, off the frame path; buildCellEntry now skips the body for those cells (ore keeps its crystals as a React overlay). Scrolling the window rewrites matrices and counts only, mounting and unmounting nothing. Materials are the existing uniform-tinted singletons and the per-cell tint jitter already rides positionWorld (which includes the instance transform), so the blocks render pixel-identical. Teetering and fallen blocks, boulders, magma, gas, part-caches, tunnels, ladders, planks, beacons, drops, bags, cracks, darkness overlays, and the dynamite charge all stay on the React path (sparse, and the teeter wobble needs per-block transforms). Changed
Resolves F-075, the reconcile half of the phone hitches (user report: "still seeing lag when falling"; telemetry showed the heap climbing 32 to 170 MB in 30 s during falls). The mine canvas rebuilt every visible cell's JSX on every store tick, so React reconciled the whole grid per action and per fall row. Cells now build through a per-cell signature cache: the cell-field fingerprint (cellRenderSignature) lives beside MineBlockBody in mine-block-render.tsx so the enumeration sits with the JSX that reads the fields, and the canvas appends its view-layer inputs (quantized darkness opacity and damage, dynamite preview, salvage and selection state, handler presence). On a signature match the tick hands React the previous element references and reconciliation bails out on the whole cell subtree; the mine world mutates in place, so object identity could never stand in for this. Click handlers dispatch through a ref (cached elements never hold a stale prop), the teeter mount ref is a stable callback with wobble targets refreshed per render, the builder sits at module scope so cached closures cannot pin the render scope that built them, and eviction sweeps cells that left the window by render generation instead of dumping the live set. Also fixed the heap-churn probe: headless Chrome freezes performance.memory without --enable-precise-memory-info, so the probe measured nothing silently; it now passes the flag and warns on a flat heap.

Passed: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit; pnpm test (995); Biome on touched files; pnpm build; dash and git diff --check; Playwright mine-core, mine-ui, mine-viewport, mine-navigation (36 passed) before the review pass and re-run after it. codex/google-account-sync-design
PR
Pending.
Changed
Added a typed provider readiness object to the account status path while keeping the existing providerReady boolean for compatibility. The no-SDK account resolver now reports Clerk as { ready: false, reason: "sdk_not_wired" }, /api/account/status returns that as providerStatus, the client parser preserves it with a fallback for older responses, the store carries it through account state, and the Account dialog requires both the legacy boolean and the explicit provider status before enabling Google sign-in. Menu lift: the bot rises above an open sheet (slice O)

Branch
workshop-o-lift, from origin/main. Verified on a temporary CI branch, then fast-forwarded to main.
PR
None (direct main). Direct response to follow-up feedback after trying slice N: "we definitely need to move the bot and displayed part higher when larger menus are open."
Changed
When a tall menu sheet is open (Tune/Garage/Shop), the bot now lifts up into the band between the top header and the sheet, instead of hiding behind the sheet. Implemented as a camera view offset, not a camera move: a new MenuLift component in src/components/workshop-canvas.tsx calls camera.setViewOffset to shift the rendered image upward by a fraction of the viewport. Because the offset lives in the projection matrix, raycasting (drag targeting) stays consistent with what is drawn. src/components/workshop-panel.tsx computes the lift from the open sheet's measured content height (taller menu covers more, so it lifts more), centering the bot in the band between the header and the sheet top, and passes it as the menuLift prop. The lift is forced to zero on the Build tab and whenever the sheet is collapsed, so the hero-drag band and its pinned screen coordinates never move. The applied lift is published on the canvas dataset.menuLift for tests. UI-only: no SIM_VERSION/MINE_VERSION change. Package version 0.1.196.
Verification
Dash check, git diff --check, tsc, Biome. The scripted 390x760 probe (scripts/playtest-sheet.mjs) now asserts the lift too: Build lift is exactly 0 and the Garage lift is 0.165 (>0.05), with zero console errors. Before/after captures reviewed by eye confirm the visible pixels move: the bot goes from mostly behind the Garage sheet to fully framed above it, clear of the header (Rule 10, pixel movement confirmed visually; a WebGL framebuffer read is not reliable across the WebGPU fallback, so the automated guard is the projection param that feeds setViewOffset). New e2e "the bot lifts above an open menu sheet (O)" asserts dataset.menuLift is 0 on Build/collapsed and >0.05 on Garage. Full 17-test workshop.spec.ts green (the drag tests still pass because they drag with the sheet collapsed, lift 0). Release-note plumbing updated across the four files and the fresh-browser e2e re-run against a fresh prod build. Full unit suite green.
Assumptions
The lift is capped at 0.22 of the viewport and only applies on the menu tabs, because those are the "larger menus" the feedback named and the Build hero/carousel are canvas overlays whose screen anchors must stay fixed. A view offset was chosen over a camera move so drag raycasting stays correct and the fixed-camera drag e2e keep their pinned coordinates. Rule 13: mine tips reviewed, no change (no mine rule touched). Rule 14: stamp review done, none added (a camera-framing refinement is not a milestone).

Held-Input Cadence Survives Timer Jitter

Direct push to main under the user-directed test-locally-then-push flow, following the PR #84 merge.

None (direct main). Originated from full-matrix round 3 on the #84 branch.
Changed
Product fix in src/components/mine-input-cadence.ts: the held-input repeat chain died silently when a repeat timer fired a hair before its due time (the time guard rejected the attempt and the chain never rescheduled), which is why held digs stalled partway on loaded devices and CI runners. Test-side: the crush test drops a redundant post-activation camera poll that raced the playback's end, and the raid XP retry window widens to the same stall allowance as its siblings. No version bumps (input reliability fix; MINE_VERSION 48, SIM_VERSION 3, package 0.1.153 unchanged).

Fix No-Claim-On-File When Embedded In A Cross-Site Iframe

Branch
fix/embedded-iframe-claim-cookie
PR
#67
Changed
selling at the Assay Office while the game ran embedded in VibeCoded.games (an iframe loading vibe-bots.vercel.app under a different top-level site) failed with "no claim on file" (user-reported). Root cause: the vb_player identity cookie was SameSite=Lax, which browsers exclude from every request whose frame ancestry is cross-site, including the iframe's own same-origin fetches. With no cookie, getOrCreatePlayerId minted a fresh player on each call, so the cash-out POST ran as a new player with no mine_worlds row. The cookie is now SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned (CHIPS), so it flows in the embedded context, partitioned per top-level site, which browsers that block unpartitioned third-party cookies still accept. File: src/server/player.ts.
Verification
dash check, git diff --check, tsc --noEmit, biome check on the changed file. The fix is a cookie attribute change verified by reasoning against the SameSite and CHIPS specs; behavioral proof needs an HTTPS preview embedded cross-site (a Secure cookie will not set over http://localhost).
Assumptions
identity is partitioned per embedding host: a guest playing standalone and the same guest playing embedded get separate claims, which is consistent with guest-first identity (F-003) and unavoidable given modern browser storage partitioning.
GDD coverage
no coverage rows flipped; added a Build log entry to docs/gdd/06-mining.html (persistent claim, REQ-026).
Followups
none.

Combat Legibility (fun-factor audit response)

Branch
feature/combat-legibility
PR
pending
Changed
response to the first VibeReview playtest (session docs/reviews/20260610-220517-4C845606), which found 60s exhibition matches ending with both bots at 100% hull. Root causes found by force probes: wheels (radius 0.4) protruded past the core face and ate every frontal contact below threshold; bots could not steer, so after the first clash they drifted onto parallel tracks and never re-engaged; the first impact burst was the only damage source (one-shot or nothing). Landed: weapon-first differential-drive steering (quaternion-rotated facing, cross-product steer, behind-hemisphere turns, all pure arithmetic), ram cycles (charge, back off, re-charge), damage restricted to bot-versus-bot contacts, weapon damage multiplier (x6), per-event damage cap (45) so the opening clash cannot one-shot, retuned threshold (20 N) and scale (0.22) from measured force distributions, wheel radius 0.34, core durability 180, SIM_VERSION 2. Second stock design (Brawler) because identical mirror bots always draw; the exhibition is now Brawler vs Rammer with design-name HUD labels, per-part damage pips, and timeout banners showing the deciding totals (epsilon-close totals are honest draws).
Verification
dash check, purity check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test (34; new stock-matchup test asserts the fight is destructive: Brawler loses over 20% of total durability and the Rammer wins), pnpm build, pnpm test:e2e. Tuning probes ran full 3600-tick matches against measured force distributions.
Assumptions
ground and self contacts deal no damage until arena hazards exist; per-event cap 45 trades guaranteed part destruction for multi-clash fights (F-007 stays open); steering gain 2, backoff 60 ticks at 0.8 speed.

Match End and Scoring

PR
pending
Changed
matches now resolve (REQ-005): a 60-second default time limit (configurable per match) with score-based judgment on timeout; end status carries the reason (disable or timeout) plus both score cards. Self-review reshaped the score model: contact damage is symmetric between the two parts in a contact, so naive dealt/taken terms cancel; the deciding terms are now remaining health ratio, parts ratio, directional pressure (in range AND closing on the enemy), and mobility at end. Damage clamps to health actually removed (overkill and debris hits pay nothing; damagePart returns the applied amount). src/sim/rewards.ts adds the deterministic reward computation from Q-002 (outcome pay table plus capped damage bonus). New shared vec3Distance helper. Also closes the combat dot file duplicate left by the PR #3 merge sequence.

Assumptions
damage tuning is measured, not guessed: starter-bot rolling forces peak near 26 N and ram/shove contact near 49 N, so the threshold is 35 N with 0.02 damage per excess newton (sustained shoving grinds parts down over seconds); constants still get a fun-factor pass later. A detached part keeps its own children attached to it (debris clusters); mobility parts riding detached debris do not count toward mobility; both bots disabled in one tick is a draw. Self-review fixes: match-scoped catalog (not the global) drives the mobility rule, axle connectors sit outboard so detachment cannot fire a depenetration damage spike into the core, removed joints are purged from every joint list, and freeMatch releases the WASM event queue.
